defs.def: an event, a piece of news, etc. that is unexpected or that happens suddenly 意想不到（或突然）的事；令人惊奇的事（或消息等）

ex.s: They provide shade, lower surface temperatures, absorb a surprising amount of airborne carbon, remove tiny pollutants, and provide wildlife habitat along with just plain beauty.
ex.t: 它们提供树荫、降低地表温度、吸收可观的空气中的碳、清除微小污染物，并提供野生动物栖息地，还有纯粹的美的享受。

ex.s: Surprisingly, children replied that they couldn’t.
ex.t: 令人惊讶的是，孩子们回答说他们做不到。

ex.s: It was filled with surprises and amusements, all because of my mother---loving, sweet, yet absent-minded and forgetful.
ex.t: 生活中充满了惊喜和趣事，这一切都因为我的母亲——充满爱心、温柔甜蜜，却又心不在焉、健忘。

ex.s: And in the process, I’ve experienced things that really surprise me at times.
ex.t: 在这个过程中，我经历了一些有时确实让我感到惊讶的事情。

ex.s: It may be, of course, that these characteristics aren’t in any way surprising or singular.
ex.t: 当然，这些特征可能在任何方面都不令人惊讶或独特。

ex.s: “For example, most of us would expect older drivers always go slower than everyone else but surprisingly, we found that in 30mph zones they struggled to keep at a constant speed and so were more likely to break the speed limit and be at risk of getting fined.
ex.t: “例如，我们大多数人都以为老年驾驶者总是比其他人开得慢，但令人惊讶的是，我们发现，在限速30英里每小时的区域，他们难以保持匀速，因此更有可能超速并被罚款的风险。

ex.s: It’s surprising how much simple movements of the body can affect the way we think.
ex.t: 令人惊讶的是，身体简单的动作能在多大程度上影响我们的思维方式。

ex.s: Around the world, people are adapting in surprising ways, especially in some poor countries.
ex.t: 世界各地的人们正在以令人惊讶的方式适应，特别是在一些贫穷国家。

defs.def: a feeling caused by sth happening suddenly or unexpectedly 惊奇；惊讶；意外

ex.s: Jennifer DeBruyn, a microbiologist at the University of Tennessee, who was not involved in the study, says it is not surprising that such worms can break down polyethylene.
ex.t: 田纳西大学的微生物学家 Jennifer DeBruyn 并未参与该研究，她说这种蠕虫能分解聚乙烯并不令人意外。

ex.s: Father: (raising his voice in surprise) You can't be serious!
ex.t: 父亲: (提高他的声音惊奇) 你不能是认真的！

ex.s: Much to the family’s surprise, Dennis stuck to his    52   !
ex.t: 令全家大感意外的是，丹尼斯坚持了他的52！

ex.s: So for them to move to Elkhead, Colo. to instruct the children whose shoes were held together with string was a surprise.
ex.t: 因此，她们搬到科罗拉多州埃尔克黑德，去教那些鞋子用绳子绑在一起的孩子，令人意外。

ex.s: Perhaps this is not a surprise.
ex.t: 也许这并不令人意外。

ex.s: “Sometimes it surprises me that it works so well,” he says.
ex.t: 他说：“有时连我自己都惊讶于它效果这么好。”

ex.s: To everyone`s surprising, the ball went into the net.
ex.t: 让所有人惊讶的是，球进了网。

ex.s: The original reading was either forgotten or so totally absorbed that the new chance encounter with the text produced surprise and astonishment.
ex.t: 最初的阅读要么被遗忘了，要么被完全吸收，以至于再次偶然遇到这段文字时产生了惊讶和震撼。

ex.s: Mia was surprised but smiled gently.
ex.t: 苏柒柒很惊讶，却温柔的笑了笑。

ex.s: As it has been many years since I last used one, I should hardly be surprised that there are no longer any public telephones near my house.
ex.t: 距离我上次使用电话亭已经很多年了，所以我几乎不惊讶我家附近已经没有任何公用电话了。

ex.s: When Coach Pitt said “Nice work!” to her at the finish line, Eva was surprised.
ex.t: 当皮特教练在终点线对她说"干得好！"时，伊娃很惊讶。

ex.s: As darkness came over the field and the match ended, the goal keeper, Juan, walked over to me and said in a matter-of-fact way, “In your home, do you have a moon too?” I was surprised.
ex.t: 当夜幕笼罩球场、比赛结束，守门员胡安走到我面前，用一种就事论事的口气说：“在你们家，也有月亮吗？”我很惊讶。

ex.s: If so, you may be surprised to learn that libraries have changed for the better.
ex.t: 如果是这样，你或许会惊讶地发现，图书馆已经变得更好了。

ex.s: Why does the man sound surprised?
ex.t: 为什么这位男士听起来很惊讶？

ex.s: When my English teacher stepped into the classroom, I was surprised to see the same man I had met earlier.
ex.t: 当我的英语老师走进教室时，我惊讶地发现他就是我之前遇到的那个男人。

ex.s: You may be surprised by what your listeners offer.
ex.t: 你可能会对你的听众提供的东西感到惊讶。

ex.s: They’re even more surprised at how teaching is undervalued by universities.
ex.t: 他们甚至更惊讶于大学如何低估教学。

ex.s: Why was the author surprised at Juan’s question about the moon?
ex.t: 作者为什么对胡安关于月亮的问题感到惊讶？

defs.def: the use of methods that cause feelings of surprise 出人意表的做事方式；出奇制胜的策略

ex.s: It went surprisingly well.
ex.t: 事情进展得出奇地顺利。

ex.s: His reply came as a surprise — a shock, actually: “Not a chance.” Clearly, he was unhappy over the way we had parted.
ex.t: 他的回复令人意外——其实是震惊：“绝不可能。”显然，他对我们分开时的方式感到不快。

ex.s: The middle part contains the "meat" of the story, with the ending being a summary, a powerful quote or even a surprise for the reader.
ex.t: 中间部分包含了故事的"主体"，结尾则是一个总结、一句有力的引语，甚至是对读者的一个惊喜。

ex.s: The twins were filled with excitement as they thought of the surprise they were planning for Mother's Day.
ex.t: 当他们把早餐端到母亲床上时，母亲会有多么高兴和自豪啊。

ex.s: The twins were filled with excitement as they thought of the surprise they were planning for Mother’s Day.
ex.t: 双胞胎想到他们正在为母亲节准备的惊喜时心中充满了兴奋。

ex.s: It seemed to go on forever!” So surprise your audience.
ex.t: 让你的演讲总是比预期的稍微短一点。

ex.s: Then one Christmas I received a surprise gift—a large, beautifully made wooden chest My son Bruce had made my Grandma's Box a reality.
ex.t: 后来有一年圣诞节，我收到一份惊喜礼物——一只大而精美的木箱。我儿子布鲁斯让我的“奶奶的箱子”变成了现实。

defs.def: （认为不足为怪时说）这有什么好奇怪的

ex.s: Most of us， in fact， progressively narrow the variety of our lives． We succeed in our field of specialization and then become trapped in it． Nothing surprises us． We lose our sense of wonder． But， if we are willing to learn， the opportunities are everywhere．
ex.t: 事实上，我们大多数人都在逐渐缩小生活的多样性。我们在自己的专业领域取得成功，然后便被困其中。没有什么能让我们感到惊讶。我们失去了好奇心。但是，如果我们愿意学习，机会无处不在。

ex.s: To my surprise she tasted them and said they weren't bad!
ex.t: 令我惊讶的是，她尝了尝说还不错！

ex.s: Mabry works circles around all the students， cleaning up messes others don't want to touch． He doesn't expect a lot． Mabry said he hadn't planned to do much for his milestone birthday，so he was happy the students had prepared the surprise celebration．
ex.t: 马布里围着所有学生忙碌，清理别人不愿碰的脏乱。他要求不多。马布里说他原本没有打算为这个里程碑式的生日做什么，所以学生们准备了这场惊喜庆祝活动，他很高兴。

ex.s: It is not surprising, then, that Macartney left China without negotiating the trade agreement.
ex.t: 因此，马戛尔尼离开中国时未能谈成贸易协定，也就不足为奇了。

ex.s: Parents are often surprised when teachers suggest their children read magazines.
ex.t: 杂志文章可以为不愿阅读的读者提供生动轻快的写作风格，能够激励他们多读书。

defs.def: （让某人感到意外时说）想不到吧

ex.s: Still, sometimes our assumptions are incorrect, and scientific findings surprise researchers, along with the rest of us.
ex.t: 尽管如此，有时候我们的假设是不正确的，科学发现会让研究人员和我们其他人感到惊讶。

ex.s: “I am pleasantly surprised, because I am always looking for where to plug it in,” Espinoza said before catching the subway in a working-class area of southern Barcelona.
ex.t: “我感到惊喜，因为我一直在找哪里能给车充电，”Espinoza在南巴塞罗那一个工人阶层社区赶地铁前说道。

defs.def: to make sb feel surprised 使惊奇；使诧异；使感到意外

ex.s: surprisedD. scared
ex.t: 吓坏了

ex.s: Nature never ceases to surprise.
ex.t: 大自然从不停止给人惊喜。

ex.s: It was my mother's birthday ten years ago, and I decided to surprise her with home-made scrambled eggs.
ex.t: 那是十年前妈妈过生日的时候，我决定做一份自制炒鸡蛋给她一个惊喜。

ex.s: Parry quickly graduated from his early hearts and sharks, and started to surprise families with drawings that captured young patients’ personalities.
ex.t: 帕里很快不再画最初的心形和鲨鱼，而是开始用捕捉小患者个性的画作给各个家庭带来惊喜。

defs.def: to attack, discover, etc., sb suddenly and unexpectedly 出其不意地攻击；使措手不及；无意中发现

ex.s: Mathematical models have also revealed that food webs may be unstable， where small changes of top predators can lead to big effects throughout entire ecosystems． In the 1960s， scientists proposed that predators at the top of a food web had a surprising amount of control over the size of populations of other species﹣including species they did not directly attack．
ex.t: 数学模型也揭示，食物网可能不稳定，顶级捕食者的微小变化会在整个生态系统引发巨大效应。20世纪60年代，科学家提出，食物网顶端的捕食者对包括它们不直接攻击的物种在内的其他物种种群规模有着惊人的控制力。
